smell: The canonical Executor.Run still buffers stdout and stderr into unbounded bytes.Buffer with no streaming option. Long-running commands routed through this wrapper (terraform apply, openshift-install create ignition-configs, helm upgrade --wait, oc get with large output) retain their entire output in RAM until the child exits. A large Proxmox terraform apply can produce tens of MB of text. The env-allowlist hardening landed in the April cycle, but streaming did not.
evidence:
var stdout, stderr bytes.Buffer
cmd.Stdin = stdin
cmd.Stdout = &stdout
cmd.Stderr = &stderr
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — the wrapper is used by every phase; long-running terraform/openshift-install paths inherit unbounded buffering with no stream option.
fix_summary: Add a RunStreaming (or Option WithStreaming) variant that tees to an io.Writer supplied by the caller (os.Stdout / slog adapter) while optionally capturing a bounded tail (e.g. last 64KB of stderr via a ring buffer) for error messages. Migrate terraform.Executor.run and the openshift-install callers in setup/ignition.go to the streaming variant; leave short-output oc callers on the buffered variant.
rule_source: Uber Go §Exec: prefer streaming for long-lived subprocesses
must_preserve: Executor.Run's (*Result, error) contract — callers read result.Stdout and result.Stderr. A streaming variant must NOT change the existing signature. Env allowlist (buildEnv) must continue to filter parent credentials.

smell: terraform Executor.run still routes init/apply/destroy through the buffered internal/executor Run — apply of a 6-VM Proxmox cluster routinely emits >10MB of progress text. A PlanStreamed variant landed for plan-only flows, but apply and destroy still buffer everything in RAM and the operator loses streaming progress feedback during a 10-minute apply. The executor-level streaming variant this needs has not landed yet (see sub:7b2829bb:unbounded-output-buffer).
severity_reason: rubric §4/canonical-helper-on-critical-path — terraform apply is the primary long-running subprocess in deploy; buffering hides progress and can OOM on large plans.
fix_summary: Once executor.Executor grows a streaming variant (see sub:7b2829bb:unbounded-output-buffer), switch terraform.Executor.run to the streaming variant with a bounded tail for stderr. Alternatively add ApplyStreamed and DestroyStreamed mirrors of PlanStreamed that call t.exec.RunInteractive for apply/destroy when a TTY is attached.
must_preserve: terraform.ExecError carries ExitCode and Stderr for typed error handling — streaming variant must still capture enough stderr for error construction. ExecError = executor.ExitError alias must stay intact.

smell: ManageService runs systemctl enable/disable/start/stop/restart/reload via exec.CommandContext(...).Run() with both stdout and stderr left nil. On failure the caller gets a bare *exec.ExitError with no systemctl diagnostic ('Failed to enable unit: Unit file haproxy.service does not exist' / 'Job for X failed because the control process exited'). This is the same stderr-dropped pattern already fixed in dnsmasq.go, firewall.go, and iface.go via system.RunCaptured — the canonical systemd wrapper is now the remaining lone offender, and it fans out to every phase (haproxy, apache, dnsmasq, cleanup).
fix_summary: Route the default (state-changing) branch through system.RunCaptured so the returned error carries systemctl's stderr diagnostic. The is-active/is-enabled probe branches can stay on bare .Run() — exit code alone is the signal and --quiet already suppresses stderr noise. After the fix, Apache / HAProxy / dnsmasq / cleanup failures will surface the upstream journalctl line instead of 'exit status 1'.
must_preserve: Non-Linux runtime.GOOS branch returning a clear error; probe-branch semantics (Run() == nil as truthy) for IsServiceActive and IsServiceEnabled; the documented fan-out shape where the caller supplies description (currently underscore in the signature).
